blocks.text: In Russian, as in English, there are verbs which can have both the direct and indirect objects (говорить, писать, читать, etc.): *Я пишу другу письмо.* — I am writing my friend a letter. In Russian, the noun denoting the indirect object (другу) is in the dative case. The dative case is used mostly to denote the person to whom something is given, sent, told, shown, etc.:
In these instances the dative case answers the questions кому? чему? The question чему? (for inanimate nouns) is seldom used.

Note. The dative case of feminine nouns which end in -ия and -ь is the same as the genitive and prepositional: *От кого это письмо? — От Марии, от дочери. Кому вы пишете? — Марии, дочери. О ком вы говорите? — О Марии, о дочери.*

The preposition по means "along" and is used with the dative case: *Я иду по коридору. Они едут по дороге.* По may mean "about", "around": *Он ходит по комнате. Они ездят по городу.* Notice also: по почте — by mail; по телефону — by phone; по радио — by radio; по делу — on business.

The preposition к (to, towards, in the direction of) always requires the dative case and is widely used with verbs of motion. After a verb of motion, к followed by a noun denoting a person indicates going to see that person at his place: *Я иду к полковнику.* Followed by a noun denoting an object or a place, it indicates motion toward that object or place: *Студент идёт к доске. Самолёты летят к морю.*
